glosses: to shovel over, to shovel across (to shovel from one place to another)
to sift through, to dig through, to pore over, to comb through, to trawl through (to look at, read or examine in large quantities)
to slog through, to crank through, to work through (to process, do or implement in large quantities)
разг. переворачивать или перебрасывать с одного места на другое (лопатой и т. п.)

examples.text: Если к осени окажется, что дернины не совсем еще перепрели, то оставляют кучу еще на год и на следующее лето опять перелопачивают.

glosses: перен., разг. просматривать, прочитывать, изучать (обычно в большом количестве)

examples.text: Крупнейшие исследовательские и биотехнологические компании, подобно старинным золотоискателям, перелопачивают сегодня генетические базы данных в поисках перспективных генов.

glosses: перен., разг. обрабатывать, делать, переделывать, осуществлять (обычно в большом количестве)

examples.text: На Раису напал трудовой зуд — это всегда случается после очередной домашней перебранки, — начала все перетряхивать, все перелопачивать: мыть полы, заново переставлять мебель, подметать заулок.

translations.source_sense_description: переворачивать или перебрасывать с одного места на другое

glosses: A hand tool with a handle, used for moving portions of material such as earth, snow, and grain from one place to another, with some forms also used for digging. In strict usage differentiated from a spade, which is designed solely for small-scale digging and incidental tasks such as chopping of small roots.

examples.text: It was said that such train crews kept a spare shovel on board because, on numerous occasions, the beginner had not only zealously thrown coal into the firebox but had let the shovel go as well.

glosses: A mechanical part of an excavator with a similar function.
Any shovel in the above senses, or any spade.
Ellipsis of shovel hat.

examples.text: No one seems to like the offer, and the umpire is just coming down, when a queer old hat, something like a doctor of divinity's shovel, is chucked on to the stage […]

glosses: To move materials with a shovel.

examples.text: The workers were shovelling gravel and tarmac into the pothole in the road.
After the blizzard, we shoveled the driveway for the next two days.
I don't mind shoveling, but using a pickaxe hurts my back terribly.
Off again, a fierce light now trailing out behind us from the open furnace door, lighting up the fireman as he shovelled more coal on to the furnace, [...].
The coal is then transferred to broad-gauge wagons for transport to Dublin. The transhipment is a rather laborious business, the coal being shovelled by hand from one wagon to another.

glosses: To move with a shoveling motion.

examples.text: Already late for work, I shovelled breakfast into my mouth as fast as possible.
The keeper then seemed to claw it out with fabulous reflexes only for TV replays to show the ball had most probably crossed the line before Forster had shovelled it away.

translations.source_sense_description: переворачивать или перебрасывать с одного места на другое

glosses: To turn over, capsize or upset.

examples.text: About three or four minutes later still an express freight on the up main line ran into the wreckage at about 35 m.p.h. Its engine also overturned and 15 more wagons were added to the mounting pile of wreckage.
We also found that the only emergency egress from the tram was by smashing the front or rear windscreens, and that emergency lighting had failed when the tram overturned.

glosses: To overthrow or destroy.
To reverse (a decision); to overrule or rescind.

examples.text: In a report for the Sun on Sunday, Barak claimed that Andrew is consulting lawyers about overturning that settlement.
Harvey was rightfully convicted. It’s unfortunate that the court has overturned his conviction. As a survivor, I am beyond disappointed.

glosses: To diminish the significance of a previous defeat by winning; to make a comeback from.

examples.text: Villa spent most of the second period probing from wide areas and had a succession of corners but despite their profligacy they will be glad to overturn the 6-0 hammering they suffered at St James' Park in August following former boss Martin O'Neill's departure

There were so many heroes for Leicester on an evening when they played with tremendous courage and belief to overturn the 2-1 deficit from the first leg, yet it was hard to look beyond Kasper Schmeichel for the game’s outstanding performer.

glosses: To undergo a limnic eruption, where dissolved gas suddenly erupts from the depths.
A turning over or upside-down; inversion.
The overturning or overthrow of some institution or state of affairs; ruin.

translations.source_sense_description: переворачивать или перебрасывать с одного места на другое

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see turn, over.

examples.text: The family feeling was intensified as we stopped to speak to mothers in the cottage gardens, or waved to distant tractors turning over chocolate-brown furrows and driven by 'my dad' or 'my Uncle Bob'.

glosses: To flip over; to rotate uppermost to bottom.

examples.text: Turn over the box and look at the bottom.
The brakes were applied immediately, but the engine ran into a sand drag at approximately 20 m.p.h., plunged down the embankment, and turned over on its side at the bottom.

glosses: To relinquish; give back.

examples.text: They turned over the evidence to the authorities.

glosses: To transfer.

examples.text: But what is to be done with our manufacturing population […] This one thing, of doing for them by ‘underselling all people,’ and filling our own bursten pockets and appetites by the road; and turning over all care for any ‘population,’ or human or divine consideration except cash only, to the winds, with a “Laissez-faire” and the rest of it: this is evidently not the thing.

glosses: To produce, complete, or cycle through.

examples.text: They can turn over about three hundred units per hour.

glosses: To generate (a certain amount of money from sales).

examples.text: The business turned over £1m last year.

glosses: To mull, ponder

examples.text: Thus they dwelled for nearly a year, and in that time Robin Hood often turned over in his mind many means of making an even score with the Sheriff

glosses: To spin the crankshaft of an internal combustion engine using the starter or hand crank in an attempt to make it run.
To give up control (of the ball and thus the ability to score).

examples.text: The Giants didn't turn the ball over in their last four games.

glosses: To cause extensive disturbance or disruption to (a room, storage place, etc.), e.g. while searching for an item, or ransacking a property.

examples.text: I've turned over the whole place, but I still can't find my glasses.
Thieves turned over the apartment while the owners were away on holiday.

examples.text: Um diesen Baum zu pflanzen, muss ich erstmal ein Loch schaufeln.
Bagger schaufeln emsig Erde auf Lastwagen.
„Wir schaufeln die Erde um – durch Landwirtschaft, durch Baumaßnahmen, durch Bergbau, so dass wir heute dreißig Mal mehr Material umverlagern, als das natürlichen Prozessen entspricht.
„Wir müssen die Zufahrt so schnell wie möglich wieder freikriegen. Bitte schaufel den Schnee aus der Einfahrt.“
Er hatte großen Hunger und schaufelte sich eine Riesenportion Kartoffelpüree auf den Teller.

glosses: große Mengen bewegen

examples.text: "Geld einfach in ein System zu schaufeln kann heißen, die Führung eines scheiternden Staates zu bestärken." sagt Collier.

glosses: Remuer à l’aide d’une pelle.

examples.text: Les graines, après être restées en tas quelques heures pendant lesquelles on les a pelletées constamment, sont placées dans un alambic […].
Un de mes cousins, qui avait alors vingt ans, alla pelleter des décombres un matin : le soir il était mort, écrasé, le sang lui sortant par les oreilles et par la bouche.

glosses: Déplacer la neige à l’aide d’une pelle.

examples.text: On peut y aller, je viens de finir de pelleter l’entrée.

glosses: Déplacer un problème, un enjeu.

examples.text: Justin Trudeau pellette aussi dans la cour des villes la responsabilité d’interdire les armes de poing. Valérie Plante n’a vraiment pas apprécié. François Legault, non plus.
D’un côté, un premier ministre qui se terre, refuse de prendre ses responsabilités et pellette son problème dans la cour de la police.
